title: The coordination of dehydration tolerance and avoidance in oaks is mediated by leaf habit across a precipitation gradient
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Forests worldwide are increasingly impacted by drought due to climate change, prompting plants to adapt through dehydration tolerance (DT) and avoidance (DA), two distinct physiological strategies. However, how these strategies are coordinated in response to varying precipitation remains unclear. To address this gap, we investigated key hydraulic traits associated with DT and DA in 11 oaks (Quercus spp.) across a broad precipitation gradient (498–1793 mm year−1) in China. Specifically, we measured three DT traits: water potential at 50% loss of hydraulic conductivity (Ψ P50), leaf turgor loss point water potential (Ψ TLP) and wood density (WD), as well as four DA traits: water potential at stomatal closure (Ψ close), minimum leaf conductance, branch capacitance and leaf-to-sapwood area ratio (A L:A S). When analysed collectively, most traits showed no significant relationship with precipitation or aridity. However, distinct patterns emerged when data were analysed by leaf habit. In evergreens, trait variation was largely and independently explained by mean annual precipitation (MAP), with stronger DT (lower Ψ P50 and Ψ TLP, higher WD) and enhanced DA (smaller A L:A S) under drier conditions. In contrast, deciduous species showed weaker DT (higher Ψ P50) but stronger DA (higher Ψ close and lower A L:A S) as precipitation decreased, with much variance driven by interactions between MAP and mean annual temperature (MAT). Notably, DT and DA traits were strongly correlated in evergreens but weakly associated in deciduous species. Our results show that evergreen oaks rely on both DT and DA strategies for drought adaptation, whereas deciduous species primarily depend on DA mechanisms. Considering DT alone is insufficient, and incorporating multiple DA strategies is essential for a mechanistic framework to understand forest responses. We highlight the need to integrate leaf habit and complementary drought strategies into predictive models and climate-resilient forest management practices.

摘要

在气候变化背景下，干旱对森林生态系统的影响日益加剧。树木主要依赖耐旱(dehydration tolerance)和避旱(dehydration avoidance)两类生理策略来应对水分胁迫。然而，树木如何协调这两类策略来适应降水变化仍不清楚。 为填补这一知识空白，本研究在中国沿降水梯度(498–1793 mm)系统测定了11种栎属植物的关键耐旱与避旱性状。具体包括3个耐旱性状:木质部导水率损失50%时的水势(Ψ P50)、叶片膨压丧失点水势(Ψ TLP)、木材密度(WD)，以及4个避旱性状:气孔关闭时的水势(Ψ close)、叶片最小导度、枝条水容、叶片与边材面积比(A L:A S)。 将所有数据放在一起分析时，多数性状与降水量或干旱程度之间无显著关联。然而，按叶片习性分组后，出现了明显分异的适应模式。常绿树种在干旱生境中表现出更强的耐旱性(更低的Ψ P50与Ψ TLP、更高的WD)与避旱性(更小的A L:A S)，其性状变异主要由年均降水量单独解释。相比之下，落叶树种在干旱地区耐旱性较弱(更高的Ψ P50)，但避旱能力显著增强(更低的Ψ close、更小的A L:A S)，其性状变异主要受年均降水量与年均温的交互作用驱动。此外，常绿树种中耐旱与避旱性状间呈现强耦合关系，而落叶树种中二者关联较弱。 综上所述，常绿栎树通过协同增强耐旱与避旱性状来适应干旱，而落叶树种主要依赖避旱策略的优化。因此，仅关注耐旱性难以完整揭示树木的干旱响应机制，将多重避旱策略纳入考量对构建更具机理性的森林干旱响应理论至关重要。本研究强调，在未来森林响应预测模型及适应性管理实践中，必须综合考虑叶片习性以及多重干旱适应策略。
